summary:
During long-duration deep-space transit, astronauts confront severe sensory deprivation, microgravity fluid shifts, and profound isolation. Due to "The Right Stuff" syndrome—the career-driven instinct to mask psychological vulnerability from flight surgeons to protect flight status—subjective self-report surveys fail.

awmeh is an edge-native, zero-intrusion behavioral health and sensory equilibrium system engineered for deep-space missions. Operating entirely on an air-gapped on-station Neural Processing Unit (NPU), awmeh continuously synthesizes passive biometric streams—vocal acoustic micro-perturbations (Jitter/Shimmer), Psychomotor Vigilance (PVT) latencies, sleep micro-architecture, and computer-vision sociometric spacing (derived from NASA OSDR datasets OSD-952, OSD-751, and OSD-738).

Crucially, raw telemetry never downlinks to Earth mission control, preserving crew autonomy and medical privacy under NASA-STD-3001. Instead, awmeh engages an autonomous closed-loop habitat countermeasure protocol, pairing environmental circadian adjustments with dual emotional anchors: Heritage Echo (auditory debriefs from Apollo/ISS commanders) and Kinship Tether (asynchronous Earth audio uplinks via Deep Space Network), maintaining psychological equilibrium across interplanetary distances.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

awmeh is an edge-native, zero-intrusion behavioral health and sensory equilibrium system for long-duration deep-space missions. It operates across a Two-Tier Architecture:

- Tier 1 (Crew Cockpit Interface):

• 5-Axis Equilibrium Radar: Real-time synthesis of Sleep, Cardio, Cognitive, Resilience, and Circadian Synchronization using clinical colors (≥80% Green Nominal, 60–79% Amber Caution, <60% Red Critical).

• Passive Biometric Quad: Tracks Heart Rate Variability (RMSSD vagal tone), Subconscious Media Valence, Galley Social Presence (markerless pose dwell time), and PVT-B Reaction Latencies.

• Interactive Voice Stress Lab: Features a real-time 60 FPS oscilloscope waveform and 64-band logarithmic FFT spectrum. Reviewers can test their own voice via microphone or analyze pre-loaded astronaut voice benchmarks and authentic NASA CHAPEA audio, calculating fundamental frequency (F0), jitter (≥1.04%), shimmer (≥3.81%), and composite vocal strain.

• Dual Emotional Anchors: Activates Heritage Echo (Apollo 13 / ISS veteran coping audio debriefs) and Kinship Tether (familial messages and Earth soundscapes time-stamped via Deep Space Network delay).

- Tier 2 (Clinical Pathophysiology Audit Modal):

• Provides Chief Medical Officers with drill-downs into spectral HRV (SDNN, LF/HF), Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter (ONSD for SANS), REM latency disinhibition (<60 min), and Slow-Wave Sleep (SWS) depletion, backed by streaming hex telemetry logs.

2. What benefits does it have?

- Zero-Burden Passive Monitoring: Crew members do not have to fill out daily psychometric questionnaires or wear intrusive clinical harnesses.

- Overcoming "The Right Stuff" Masking: Bypasses the psychological barrier where astronauts deliberately hide exhaustion or anxiety to protect flight qualification status.

- Guaranteed Medical Privacy: 100% of high-frequency raw biometrics are computed on an air-gapped on-station processor and never downlinked to Mission Control, establishing crew trust.

- In-Situ Autonomous Care: Provides closed-loop habitat adjustments (480nm photopic lighting, acoustic masking, emotional anchors) without waiting for round-trip Earth communication.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

- Deep-Space Exploration (Artemis Gateway & Mars Transit): Solves the critical barrier of round-trip communication delays (up to 44 minutes), providing true psychological self-reliance for crews.

- Terrestrial Extreme Environments: Directly applies to isolated high-stress environments on Earth where workers experience severe burnout and fear reporting vulnerability—such as Antarctic winter-over bases, submarines, offshore platforms, and intensive-care hospital staff.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

- System Architecture & Ideation: Conceived, scientifically framed, and architected 100% originally by the human team lead.

- Generative SI Implementation Tooling: Super Intelligence (SI) models were actively leveraged under our team's direct prompt engineering and iterative curation to generate code scripts, synthesize neural astronaut voice stress benchmarks, and create conceptual visual assets.

- Frontend & DSP Avionics: Pure HTML5, modern CSS3 Grid/Flexbox, HTML5 Canvas 2D API, and W3C Web Audio API (real-time normalized autocorrelation pitch tracking and logarithmic FFT). Built with zero external CDN dependencies to ensure deterministic offline execution in spacecraft avionics.

- Cloud Research Backbone: Google Cloud Platform ($200 Space Apps Partner Tier) Vertex AI and Compute Engine for ground foundation model fine-tuning on NASA analog cohorts and encrypted federated parameter sync simulations.

5. How is your project creative?

- The Triple-Soul of "awmeh":

1. Cultural & Psychological Insight: Inspired by the colloquial Malaysian expression "...meh?", reflecting the astronaut's internal defense mechanism when hiding vulnerability from flight surgeons: "I'm okay meh?", "Nothing wrong with me meh?".

2. Heartfelt Mission: It stands for "Always Mental Health"—not a punitive monitor or surveillance camera, but an invisible, non-judgmental guardian angel in the dark.

3. Formal Aerospace Acronym: On the official flight manifest, it is "Astronaut Wellbeing & Mental-health Edge Heuristics."

- The "Invisible Diagnostic" Paradigm: Extracts clinical indicators from normal daily operations (speech cadence, galley transit time, keystroke variance, sleep polysomnography) rather than artificial clinical tests.

- Dual Emotional Anchors: Reconnects the isolated human psyche through mission heritage ("Heritage Echo" normalizes crisis) and terrestrial kinship ("Kinship Tether" combats the Earth-Out-of-View phenomenon).

- Hands-on Reviewer Testing: Hackathon judges can click "Voice Stress Lab" in the live prototype to test their own vocal jitter and shimmer in real time.

6. What factors did your team consider?

- Interplanetary Latency: 3- to 22-minute one-way light delay to Mars makes ground tele-counseling impossible; all primary inference must be on-station.

- Astronaut Career Psychology: Elite crews fear being grounded; the system must be supportive, private, and non-punitive.

- Spacecraft SWaP Constraints: Stringent avionics power and memory limits required an ultra-lightweight, zero-dependency software stack.

- Sensory Monotony: Monotonous habitat environments disrupt biological clocks; awmeh automatically triggers 480nm blue light shifts and fan-whine masking.
